Nationwide, estimated overdose deaths dropped by nearly 14% last year, falling from about 81,300 deaths in 2024 to just under 70,000 in 2025. That’s the lowest national total since 2018. Arizona’s numbers are much more troubling. Estimated overdose deaths increased by 18%, rising from 2,531 in 2024 to 2,988 in 2025. The increases weren’t limited to one type of drug. Deaths involving synthetic opioids — mostly fentanyl — increased by nearly 33%. Deaths involving methamphetamine and other stimulants rose by more than 15%. sources.page_context: PM Updated: May 15, 2026, 12:31 pm 7 Follow on Google News Arizona overdose deaths rose despite a national decline, while naloxone overdose reversals increased as fentanyl, meth and other adulterated drugs fueled risk. Arizona’s overdose reversals, instances in which naloxone is used to restore breathing after an opioid overdose, nearly tripled in 2025 .
